result.summary: Built the Saathi app and the Impact and Compliance screens on top of the lead's latest commit. The worktree started at 1403f83 (main) without the prototype foundation, so I fast-forwarded the branch to feat/prototype dfd8c19 before starting; the other worktrees 012-1 to 012-8 were also at 1403f83 when checked. Backend: convex/saathi.ts has board (open jobs city-wide with the Saathi's own area first, their assigned jobs, finished jobs and earnings, each with the posting business), take (open to assigned to me; refuses a taken job, a past-dated job and a double-booked slot) and finish (assigned to me to done; refuses someone else's job, a job already done and finishing before the job's day). Both mutations write auditLog. convex/insights.ts has impact, a union on kind: for a business, kilos from households, bought and sold in completed trades, kilos recycled counted once per material family (the larger of in and out, CO2e taken from the same side), CO2e from the materials table, money earned and spent, and a by-family breakdown; for a Saathi, jobs done, earnings, earnings by kind of work and recent jobs. It also has compliance: GSTIN, consent status (ok / expiring under 90 days / expired / missing) with days left and a reminder date, a checklist (GST, consent, Legal Metrology scale stamp and safety kit, the last two self-declared), trade invoices with e-way bill flags, and the April-to-March EPR record for recyclers and manufacturers by stream (PWM Rules 2016, E-Waste Rules 2022, Battery Waste Management Rules 2022; batteries split out of e-waste; none for paper, metal and glass) with a note that certificates are generated on CPCB's EPR portals. The pure rules are exported and unit-tested. UI: SaathiHome (this week's pay card, today's jobs with a confirmed Mark done, jobs coming up, open jobs with Take, icons for kind of work and time of day, 48px targets); ImpactPage (KPIs chosen per business kind, a plain-div bar chart by material using the chart-3 token, which passes the dataviz palette checks, in and out flows, the credit-ready ledger explainer; Saathis see earnings and finished jobs); CompliancePage (consent validity card with reminder or renew / expired alerts, the checklist with a 'what this means' note per item, invoices as cards on phones and a table on wide screens linking to /app/trades/{id}/invoice, the EPR summary; Saathis are pointed back to their jobs). All three have skeletons, empty states, an error boundary with retry, toast plus inline errors, and one DemoNote each. Tests: 35 convex-test cases (board contents, take and finish rules, refusals for signed out, wrong role and someone else's job, exact impact numbers on the demo world, consent math including the last day and a leap year, the financial-year boundary, consent expiring and expired on data) and 35 component and unit tests. The Date object is frozen at 29 Sep 2026 in the Convex tests so they stay deterministic.
routes: /app (Saathi home, rendered by RoleHome for Saathis)

The kabadiwala's app is built: home, pickup requests, weigh and pay, stock and prices. It is one commit on top of the lead's dfd8c19. Typecheck and ESLint pass on every file I touched. The 79 tests for this area pass; the only failing test in the full suite is src/i18n/messages.test.ts, which waits on translations. I could not open the screens in a browser, because running the dev server was ruled out.

Backend:
- convex/shop.ts: every function starts with requireOrg(ctx, ['kabadiwala']).
  - requests: new / active / done, with done capped at the latest 20.
  - get: one booking plus the shop's rate for each item. It returns null for another shop's booking or a bad id.
  - respond and startTrip: status moves checked with canMoveBooking, added to the timeline and written to auditLog. startTrip refuses drop-offs.
  - complete: prices each line at the rate card, else the city fallback, with paiseFor. It saves the receipt with the rate used, sets points with pointsFor, marks the booking completed and adds the grams to inventory (upsert by_org_material).
  - rateCard and setRate: setRate refuses a price under the floor with BELOW_FLOOR and writes an audit row.
  - payouts (extra): paid today and over the last 7 days, for the home screen.
- Privacy: until the shop accepts, it gets the first name, only the area and a masked phone. The tracking token is also blanked, because the tracking page shows the address.
- convex/stock.ts: stock.mine works for any business kind. It returns stock with names, stage, grams, value at today's market price, totals and who the business sells to.

Screens (src/components/shop), mobile first:
- KabadiwalaHome: the five placeholders replaced by real screens with the same names and props.
  - Greeting, a big count of new requests with a button to /app/requests.
  - Today's pickups with the next one (time and area).
  - Paid today and last 7 days, stock worth, a three-material price check against the market.
  - Shortcuts to /app/sell and /app/prices.
- RequestsPage: New / Today / Done tabs, kept in ?tab=.
  - Cards show first name, area, slot, items with estimated kg, and the estimate.
  - Accept is one tap; Decline asks for confirmation.
- RequestDetail:
  - Call and Directions appear once accepted; Start trip for pickups.
  - Weigh and pay: kg rows prefilled with the estimate, half-kilo steps, add another material, a live total, Cash or UPI.
  - After confirming, a receipt with a thank-you and the points earned, plus the booking history.
- StockPage: every business kind, grouped into scrap and recycled when a business holds both. The Sell button appears when buyerKindFor gives someone to sell to.
- RateCardPage: prices grouped by family, edited in place next to the minimum and market price, with a clear error below the minimum.
- Every screen has loading, empty, error and not-for-this-role states, and one sample-data note.
- All copy is in the "shop" namespace.

Tests:
- convex-test: happy paths, privacy before and after accepting, blocked status moves, the floor, receipts that later price changes don't rewrite, stock totals, and refusals for signed-out users, other roles and another shop's booking.
- Component tests with Testing Library, plus unit tests for the kg and rupee parsing.

result.summary:
I built the business-to-business market for the prototype: buying, selling, trades with simulated escrow, printable trade receipts, and the home screen for yards, recyclers and manufacturers. It is one commit (825a1d5) on top of the lead's latest commit, dfd8c19. The worktree started on main (1403f83), which doesn't have the foundation code, so I fast-forwarded it onto feat/prototype before writing anything. Typecheck, ESLint and Prettier are clean, and all 86 tests in this area pass (19 backend, 67 UI). I did not run the app or a browser, as instructed.

Backend, `convex/market.ts`: every function starts with `requireOrg`.
- **browse**: open lots from the business type below yours in the chain, in your city, never your own, newest first. Kabadiwalas get WRONG_ROLE, because they don't buy on the market.
- **myListings** lists your lots, open ones first. **sellable** is a helper the task didn't list: it tells the Sell form how much of each material is free to sell.
- **createListing** and **withdraw**: only for business types someone buys from. Weight and price must be whole numbers above zero, the weight must fit in free stock, and the note is at most 140 characters.
- **requestTrade**: only the right buyer type, with 0 < grams ≤ what's left in the lot, at the asking price.
- **trades**: a buying list and a selling list, each with the next actions, the other business, and escrow and e-way-bill flags.
- **act** moves a trade one step:
  - accept takes the weight off the lot and marks it sold at zero;
  - pay gives the receipt number LG-yy-nnnn and holds the money in escrow;
  - dispatch takes the seller's stock, and refuses if there isn't enough;
  - confirm adds the buyer's stock and releases the escrow.
  Every step adds a timeline entry and an audit-log row, and stock changes are logged too.
- **receipt** is visible to either side of the trade and returns nothing for anyone else or for a bad link. It is labelled a "Trade receipt", not a GST invoice.

Choices that go slightly beyond the task:
- **Free stock**: a new listing is checked against stock minus open listings minus sold lots not yet dispatched, not just total stock, so the same kilos can't be sold twice.
- **Closed lots**: withdrawing a lot, or selling it out, automatically declines the requests still waiting on it. While reviewing I caught and fixed a bug where selling a lot out also wrote a false "declined" log entry for the order that sold it; a test now covers this.
- **Suggested price**: scrap uses today's market price × CHAIN_MARKUP. Recycled material (flakes, granules, kraft, ingots) is not marked up again, because its market price is already the price a factory pays.
- **Receipt numbers**: finding the next number reads every trade. That's fine at pilot volume; a counter row would replace it later.
- **Lint exception**: I added one justified line-level lint exception on `createListing`, because the task names it that way and the rule doesn't fit Convex functions.

Screens, in `src/components/market`:
- **Home**: a greeting and four numbers: money in escrow, trades waiting for you, lots on sale (recycled lots on offer for manufacturers), and trades done this month. Below them, a "Waiting for you" list with one-tap buttons, then the latest lots. Manufacturers see recycled material first.
- **Buy**: material filter chips, lot cards, and a Buy dialog that shows the total as you type the weight.
- **Sell**: a new-listing form showing free stock and the suggested price, plus your listings with a Withdraw button.
- **Trades**: Buying and Selling tabs for yards and recyclers, and a single list for kabadiwalas and manufacturers. Each trade shows a five-step timeline, an escrow badge, the e-way-bill note, the next step as the main button, and a receipt link.
- **Receipt**: printable, with print styles scoped to that page, so the app shell doesn't need changes.
- Every screen has loading, empty and error states. English copy is under the `market` namespace in `messages/en.json`.

Tests:
- **Full trade on demo data**: yard 102 buys from kabadiwala 101's lot through to delivery, and stock moves on both sides.
- **Refusals**: signed out, wrong role, wrong buyer type, wrong side, someone else's trade, too much weight, not enough stock.
- **Browse**: the right tier only, and only your city.
- **UI**: unit tests for the pure logic, and component tests for the home, market and trades pages, the buy dialog, the listing form, the trade card and the receipt.

result.summary:
Admin console built end to end: verification queue, decisions, private files, price tables and support inbox.

Backend:
- convex/review.ts has four functions, all behind requireAdmin:
  - queue: applications in review, oldest first, then those sent back for changes. Each row has name, contact, phone, area, hours waiting, SLA (ok / due_soon / overdue, using the lifecycle.ts constants), file count and version.
  - summary: the counts for the home page and the menu.
  - get: the form by section, active files, login phone, number of earlier versions, which fields changed since the last version, and the application's audit trail.
  - decide: approve, ask for changes or reject, checked with canMove. Changes and reject need a note of 5+ characters. Approving creates the org (unique slug, area, consent, families, pickups), the owner membership and, for a kabadiwala, a rate card at the city fallback prices; for a Saathi it creates the saathiProfile. Approving a suspended application switches its org back on instead of creating a second one. Every decision and every org/Saathi creation is written to auditLog.
- convex/lib/review.ts (new, pure) holds the rules both server and UI use: SLA, note check, application→org/Saathi mapping, area and slug, version diff, price validation.
- convex/adminPrices.ts: list and set. Set checks whole paise, 0 < floor ≤ fallback and a ₹10,000/kg cap, and writes the old values to auditLog. Raising a floor also lifts shop prices below it (pricing.md rule 2).
- Private files: GET and OPTIONS /files/{fileId} added to convex/http.ts, backed by convex/files.ts. The caller sends the Convex token as a Bearer header and is checked with authComponent.safeGetAuthUser. Only the admin (ADMIN_EMAIL with an authenticator) or the uploader gets the file; otherwise 401/403/404. Responses are Cache-Control: private, no-store, with CORS for SITE_URL and EXTRA_TRUSTED_ORIGINS. The permission, CORS and content-disposition checks are pure functions with unit tests.

UI (English, inline copy, next/link):
- /admin/verification: table on desktop, cards on phones. SLA badges and waiting times update every minute, and there is a separate "With the applicant" section.
- /admin/verification/[id]:
  - details by section, with "Changed" markers and a consent-expiry warning
  - file viewer: gets the Convex token via authClient.convex.token(), fetches through TanStack Query, shows images inline and PDFs in an iframe via object URLs; videos load only when clicked
  - per-role checklist from onboarding.md; Approve stays disabled until every item is ticked
  - dialogs for approve / ask for changes / reject (note required for the last two); after a decision it returns to the queue with a toast
- /admin/prices: editable ₹/kg floor and fallback per material, grouped by family, with inline validation, Undo and a DemoNote.
- /admin/support: Open / Answered / All tabs, call links, mark answered.
- Console shell: Verification, Prices and Support are live nav items with counts. The home page shows waiting, overdue and open support requests. Console pages have an error boundary.

Tests (122 in 17 files for this area, all passing):
- convex-test covers queue ordering and SLA, summary, get, decide (including every refusal), adminPrices and the HTTP file route (200/401/403/404, CORS, preflight).
- Unit and component tests cover the rest of the UI logic.

Nothing was browser-tested: no dev server or Playwright, as instructed.

result.summary:
The household area is built and committed: /sell (a public page, in the sitemap) and /t/{token} (a private tracking page in the new (household) route group). Lint, typecheck and my 96 tests all pass. I couldn't run the app, so nothing has been checked in a browser yet.

My worktree branch started at 1403f83, which doesn't have the prototype foundation (schema, lib/chain, lib/workspace, the app components). I fast-forwarded it to feat/prototype dfd8c19 before building. The other seven worktree branches started at 1403f83 too.

Backend, in convex/households.ts:
- shops (public): every active kabadiwala in Bengaluru, with what that shop would pay for the basket. It uses the shop's own rates and the city fallback price for anything the shop hasn't priced, and lists those fallback items. Shops come nearest first when a location is given, otherwise best offer first. Each shop has its area, address, hours and whether it picks up.
- book: needs a signed-in household with a phone on its profile. It checks the basket (1–20 items, each over 0 and up to 500 kg, scrap materials only), the shop, the mode (a pickup needs an address and a shop that picks up), a day from today to 7 days ahead, and that the chosen time hasn't passed. It cleans up the name and address, allows at most 5 open bookings per household, creates a 'requested' booking with its estimate and timeline, writes an audit row, and returns the token.
- track (public by token): status, timeline, items and receipt lines with material names, estimate, points, and the shop's name, area, address, hours and phone. It never returns the household's phone, address or name. It also says whether the viewer is the household that booked, and whether the booking can still be cancelled.
- mine: the signed-in household's bookings, newest first; null when signed out.
- cancel: only the household that booked, and only while it is requested or accepted; writes an audit row.

The rules shared by server and UI live once in a new pure file, convex/lib/households.ts.

/sell is a 4-step flow; the step is kept in the address (?step=…) so the phone's back button goes back a step.
1. What do you have: materials grouped by family, each family with its own colour and icon, and today's price per material. Tap a material to add it, then set the kilos with − / + (it becomes "remove" at the smallest amount), a box to type in, or one-tap amounts. A running estimate and a Next button stay stuck to the bottom of the screen.
2. Who buys it: pickup or drop-off, then the shops with their offers, "Best price" and "Nearest" badges and an optional "Use my location". Shops that don't pick up can't be chosen for a pickup, with a note saying why.
3. When: the next 7 days that still have a time open, morning/afternoon/evening with times that have passed closed off, then the address (pickup) or the shop's address and hours (drop-off), and the household's name. Anything missing is pointed out when they try to go on.
4. Book: a summary with a Change link per section, the money and recycle points, then the phone. A signed-in household taps Book; anyone else enters their number and the SMS code inline, and the booking is made as soon as the code is accepted. They then land on /t/{token}. If the server refuses, the message comes with a "Fix it" link to the right step.

The basket and answers are kept in session storage until booking, so a reload or a language switch keeps them. Households who have booked before see "Your bookings" at the top of /sell.

/t/{token} shows:
- a status hero whose headline and progress bar update live as the shop answers
- when, and whether it's a pickup or drop-off
- the shop, with a Call button
- the estimate, or once weighed, the receipt with what was paid, how, and the points
- what's being collected, and the history
- Cancel: the household confirms first; someone with only the link confirms their number by SMS inside the dialog
- after a decline, "Try another shop" reloads the same scrap into /sell
- a friendly not-found page for a bad link

Pages with prices say once that they are sample data (DemoNote).

Tests: convex-test for every function (happy paths plus signed out, wrong shop, someone else's booking, the date/kg/address/name rules, the open-booking limit, and a check that no phone or address leaks from track). Component tests cover the kg stepper, grid, shop list, "When?" step and tracking page. One test drives the whole flow from basket to booking.

result.summary:
Built the help centre for every user, plus a set of 12 illustrations. It is public and indexed, and every page sets its metadata through pageMetadata.

Pages:
- /help: search across all guides and questions in the browser, one-tap topic filters (12 topics), six role cards with pictures, and a call / WhatsApp / write strip.
- /help/[role] (household, kabadiwala, yard, recycler, manufacturer, saathi): guides, questions as a native details/summary list, video slots marked "Video coming soon", and a training path. Search results that link to a question open it.
- Training: 3–5 lessons per role, each marked done with a checkbox. Progress is kept in localStorage under luma.help.training.<role>; storage access is guarded and falls back to memory if blocked. Shows a progress bar and a completion badge.
- /help/[role]/[guide]: numbered steps, each with a picture or icon (picture first on phones), related questions, the next guide, and a contact strip that pre-fills role and topic.
- /help/contact: name, phone (+91), role, topic and message, sent to api.support.send. Role and topic are read from ?role= and ?topic=. Server refusals show on the right field, success moves focus to a confirmation, and 'Send another' keeps the name and number. Quick call / WhatsApp buttons, hours, 'we reply within one working day', and the placeholder number +91 80 0000 0000 marked with DemoNote.

Content: typed data in src/components/help/content.ts (30 guides with 138 steps, 50 questions, 17 video slots, 20 lessons; guides and questions shared across roles where the flow is the same). Copy is short and plain, checked against docs/product and the lead's chain rules: floor price, 12–24 hour verification, SMS code valid 5 minutes with resend after 30 seconds, 1 point per ₹10, escrow steps, e-way bill over ₹50,000, masked Aadhaar only, and data kept for 12 months / 90 days / 30 days.

Illustrations: src/components/illustrations holds 12 original flat SVGs on a shared 240×180 frame, coloured only with token classes (brand, stone, amber, orange, sky). They are hidden from screen readers unless given a title, and are exported by name plus an `illustrations` lookup and `IllustrationName` type for other areas.

I checked the pages visually at 375px and 1280px by rendering them in jsdom with the compiled Tailwind CSS. As a result, role and video cards are now compact rows on phones, the training list is width-capped, and the message counter sits beside the error.
